messages.subject: Specify R version with specific packrat projects
messages.subject_clean: Specify R version with specific packrat projects
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to save certain projects in RStudiowith specific R versions? I have some projects I need to run in R version 3.1.x and others that require 3.2.x. After I set up each project with packrat, I ran into trouble upon opening projects of different R versions. RStudio remembers the last R version you were in, so using packrat I was forced to reinstall packages that I had running in my 3.1.x library to 3.2.x, subsequently breaking some projects, just upon opening RStudio. I have since stopped using packrat but would like to use it to preserve R versions and package versions. Thanks for any tips.

Cheers,
Emma

messages.subject: Re: Specify R version with specific packrat projects
messages.subject_clean: Specify R version with specific packrat projects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emma,

Unfortunately, RStudio doesn't yet automatically select the marked version of R for a packrat project -- you need to do it by hand. If you're using Windows, one option is to use 'Ctrl + Click' when launching RStudio, and then choose the appropriate version of R according to the project you're going to work in, but I admit this is a bit clumsy.

I'll add a note on the RStudio side to see if we can make this possible in the future.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.body_plain:
I'm still trying to get my head around how Packrat works. I initially added packrat/src to my .gitignore because I didn't want the tarball sources in the repo. That caused problems because the system got hung up when trying to install some packages (`mnormt`, for instance). So I thought thought that maybe if I added packrat/src to the repo, then I could get around the problem. However, the system is still freezing up when installing the package (and messages in the console are telling me that the binaries for other packages are being downloaded. I checked the packrat.opts and `vcs.ignore.src` is set to FALSE.  Am I missing something obvious?

Thanks in advance,
Joe

messages.subject: Re: Confused about packrat/src
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

Roughly speaking, 'snapshot()' is used to 'save' the state of your
library -- packrat looks at the active library paths, and downloads
package sources for all packages available. 'restore()' will 'load'
that state, attempting to reinstall all packages from the last
snapshot. This is done from CRAN binaries if available, and from
sources if not.

The error you saw for mnormt:

    gfortran-4.8   -fPIC  -g -O2  -c biv-nt.f -o biv-nt.o
    make: gfortran-4.8: No such file or directory

implies that packrat was attempting to install the package from
source. In this case, it requires gfortran to be available on the
system, to compile some bundled FORTRAN files in the package. Guessing
that you are on OS X, you likely need to install Xcode to get access
to clang (for compilation of C / C++ source code in packages), as well
as the gfortran-4.8 package distributed by Simon Urbanek here:

    http://r.research.att.com/libs/gfortran-4.8.2-darwin13.tar.bz2

So, my best guess is that you need to make sure compilers / Xcode are
available and installed on your system.

Thanks,
Kevin

> >> Hi Joe,
> >>
> >> Roughly speaking, 'snapshot()' is used to 'save' the state of your
> >> library -- packrat looks at the active library paths, and downloads
> >> package sources for all packages available. 'restore()' will 'load'
> >> that state, attempting to reinstall all packages from the last
> >> snapshot. This is done from CRAN binaries if available, and from
> >> sources if not.
> >>
> >> The error you saw for mnormt:
> >>
> >>     gfortran-4.8   -fPIC  -g -O2  -c biv-nt.f -o biv-nt.o
> >>     make: gfortran-4.8: No such file or directory
> >>
> >> implies that packrat was attempting to install the package from
> >> source. In this case, it requires gfortran to be available on the
> >> system, to compile some bundled FORTRAN files in the package. Guessing
> >> that you are on OS X, you likely need to install Xcode to get access
> >> to clang (for compilation of C / C++ source code in packages), as well
> >> as the gfortran-4.8 package distributed by Simon Urbanek here:
> >>
> >>     http://r.research.att.com/libs/gfortran-4.8.2-darwin13.tar.bz2
> >>
> >> So, my best guess is that you need to make sure compilers / Xcode are
> >> available and installed on your system.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Sorry to keep being a pain. I wasn't sure whether this would be of use to anyone or not.

I stared getting these errors:

```No DESCRIPTION file at path '/Users/josephflanagan/Downloads/jflanaga-d2-e-proceedings-b2d513092cca/packrat/lib/x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0/3.2.4/lazyeval/DESCRIPTION'!```

I've figured out what I need to do to fix it. First, I have to close the project and then reopen. Then, I install whatever package I get this error for (on this machine, it is pretty consistently `lazyeval` and `dplyr`. Then packrat::restore() works fine (the packages I added get ignored).

I noticed that versions of `dplyr` and `lazyeval` I have in the packrat library are the github versions (as is the packrat version). So I downgraded them to CRAN, deleted the packrat/lib directories, and opened up the project. Sure enough, everything went smoothly, except for the fact that the automatic restarted didn't boot me into the Packrat library, so I had to close the project and open it again. (and downgrading Packrat to CRAN version didn't solve that problem, but closing and opening a project isn't that big a deal).

As I said, I'm not sure if it is just my own user-error as I try to figure out how packrat works, but I thought I would report it.

of these packages without a DESCRIPTION file is getting installed and
finding its way into your library. (Or, for some reason, that
DESCRIPTION file is getting deleted?)

Were you using the latest version of packrat on GitHub when you saw
these errors? Were you running within RStudio, or in a different
environment? Do you by any chance have multiple R processes running
with the same packrat project?

Thanks,
Kevin
